title: The Anatomy of an Accessible Form 🧬
description: Labels, instructions, required fields – build the foundation of a form everyone can complete.

slides.title: Forms Are Conversations 💬
slides.content:
A form is a dialogue between the user and your site. Accessible forms make that conversation clear and frustration‑free.

* Every input must have a **label** that is programmatically associated.
* Instructions must be visible and linked via `aria-describedby`.
* Required fields must be indicated both visually and semantically.

Think of a form like a helpful shop assistant: "What's your name?", "Great, now your email address."

quizData.question: What is the most important accessibility feature for an `<input>`?
quizData.explanation: Labels are critical for screen readers to identify the input's purpose.

slides.title: Explicit vs. Implicit Labels 🏷️
slides.content:
* **Explicit**: `<label for="email">Email</label>` – best, most robust.
* **Implicit**: `<label>Email <input></label>` – can be problematic for complex layouts.
* **aria-label / aria-labelledby**: for inputs without a visible label (search icon‑only fields).

Always prefer explicit labels – they work with all assistive tech.

slides.title: Explicit Label Example
slides.codeSnippet:
<label for="email">Email address</label>
<input type="email" id="email" name="email" required>

quizData.question: Clicking on a `<label>` associated with an `<input>` should do what?

options.text: Focus or activate the associated input

quizData.explanation: It moves focus to the input (for text fields) or toggles checkboxes/radios.

slides.title: Placeholder ≠ Label ❌
slides.content:
Placeholder text disappears when the user types, often has low contrast, and is not consistently supported by screen readers.

* Use placeholder for **hints**, not labels.
* Always provide a separate visible label.

Example of a hint: `placeholder="e.g., you@domain.com"` while the label says "Email address".

slides.title: Required Fields & Instructions 📝
slides.content:
* Indicate required fields both visually (asterisk) and semantically (`required` attribute or `aria-required="true"`).
* Explain the asterisk at the top of the form (e.g., "Fields marked * are required").
* Use `aria-describedby` to link the instruction to the input.

Never rely on colour alone (red asterisk).

quizData.question: Which attribute programmatically marks a field as required?

options.text: Both A and B work; native `required` is preferred

quizData.explanation: `required` gives free browser validation; `aria-required` only informs assistive tech. Use `required`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Grouping with `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`
For sets of radios or checkboxes, wrap them in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`. The legend becomes the group label, announced for each option.
